checks: Source f1516303d16df6d4 §1 and 3795aff5f3322d52 §§2–4 support the precise localization, one-corner product formula and scalar optimization. The same argument applies to arbitrary removed shapes because only their support and volume enter each cap.

Affine normalization allows dimension-only choices. Compactness of the unit sphere and the exact centroid equality directions give a uniform positive gap away from the normal groups. Uniform vertex signs on their compact closures then include or exclude each small corner wholesale, even for nonflat deletions.

For the chosen group the cap is a corner simplex with edge fractions 1/c_j. AM–GM under sum c_j lambda_j(y)=1 gives the exact product minimum. The minimizing coefficients are strictly greater than one near the centroid, and the direction is in its designated group by continuity.

The retained centroid pays at least Gamma−t. Each canonical through-mark cap of T has fraction (1−lambda_i)^d, so every maximizing barycentric vector converges uniformly to the centroid as t decreases, and all maxima lie in the local regime. Compactness and upper semicontinuity give attainment.

At zero deletion the scalar left side is m^d D. Its derivative gives the positive local analytic root, and substituting c and the proposed coordinates makes all cap values equal D. For small losses the weights 1−d lambda_i^* are positive, sum to one, and give the exact coefficient d lambda_j^*. Strict log Jensen forces equality only at the proposed mark.
